name: Pork Chile Verde Stew

ingredients.buy: 7 lb pork shoulder, cut into 1 1/2 inch cubes
3 1/2 lb tomatillos, husked, rinsed and coarsely chopped
2 bunches fresh cilantro (reserve some for garnish)

prose.intro_html: Chile verde is what happens when a cheap, tough cut of pork meets a pot of roasted tomatillos and green chiles and nobody is in a hurry. You char the tomatillos and poblanos under the broiler, blend them into a bright green sauce, brown the pork, and let the whole thing simmer low for a couple of hours until the meat gives up and falls apart. The tomatillos do most of the seasoning work, so you are not paying for much beyond the pork and a bag of green vegetables. Built at 14 servings it comes in around {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 15 grams of carbs. That is a Sunday pot of stew that feeds you all week.
shop_smart: Seven pounds of pork shoulder is the whole recipe. This is where the money and nearly all of the protein live, and it is still one of the cheapest cuts in the case because it needs time instead of a fancy grade. Reach for a big boneless shoulder, sometimes labeled Boston butt, and cut it into large cubes yourself so you are paying for pork and not for someone else doing the trimming.

Three and a half pounds of tomatillos and seven poblano peppers are the green in chile verde. The tomatillos are the tart backbone and the poblanos are the mild green chile behind it, and together they do most of the seasoning. Buy firm tomatillos with tight, dry husks and poblanos that feel heavy and glossy, and skip the jarred salsa verde because you are building your own here.

Two bunches of cilantro, two bunches of green onions, and a head of garlic go into the blender sauce. These are what turn roasted vegetables into something that actually tastes like chile verde. The cilantro and green onions go in fresh, and you set a little cilantro aside to scatter over the top when you serve it.

Four and a half cups of chicken broth carries the braise. Half of it goes into the blender to loosen the green sauce and half thins the stew as the pork cooks down. Any plain chicken broth does the job here, so skip the bone broth and buy the everyday carton.

Cumin, chipotle powder, cinnamon, oregano, and salt are the spice shelf. A little smoked chipotle and a pinch of cinnamon are what set this version apart from a plain green stew. These are small spoonfuls from jars you likely already keep on the shelf.
make_it: Weigh your empty Dutch oven or the biggest heavy pot you own and write the number down. You will use it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight instead of guessing.

Heat the broiler. Halve the tomatillos and lay them cut side up on a sheet pan with the poblano peppers and the peeled garlic cloves tucked in among them. Broil for 5 to 6 minutes, until the tomatillos slump and the poblano skins blister and char.

Scrape everything on the pan, juices and all, into a blender. Add the cilantro, the green onions, and 2 1/4 cups of the chicken broth. Blend to a green sauce, as chunky or smooth as you like it, and set it aside.

Cut the pork shoulder into 1 1/2 inch cubes if it did not come that way, and sprinkle it all over with the salt. Heat the olive oil in the pot over high heat and brown the pork in batches, giving each batch room so it sears instead of steams. Move the browned pork to a plate.

Lower the heat to medium. Coarsely chop the yellow onions, add them to the pot, and cook about 5 minutes until they soften and turn translucent, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom as they go.

Stir in the ground cumin, chipotle powder, cinnamon, and oregano and cook one minute, until they smell toasty. Return the pork and any juices on the plate, pour in the green sauce and the remaining 2 1/4 cups broth, and bring it up to a gentle boil.

Cover the pot, drop the heat to low, and simmer 2 to 2 1/2 hours, stirring now and then, until the pork is fork-tender and the sauce has cooked down and deepened. If it ever looks too thick, loosen it with a splash of water.

Weigh the full pot and subtract the empty weight from Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide by 14 and spoon that exact weight into each container. Scatter the reserved cilantro over the top when you serve.
prose.portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide that number by 14 and spoon that exact weight into each container so every one gets the same share of pork and green sauce. Each serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

head.keywords: pork chile verde, chile verde stew, tomatillo pork stew, low carb pork dinner, high protein meal prep
steps: Weigh the empty pot and write the number down.
Broil the halved tomatillos, poblanos, and peeled garlic until charred and soft.
Blend the roasted vegetables with cilantro, green onions, and half the broth into a green sauce.
Salt and brown the cubed pork in olive oil, then set it aside.
Soften the onion, toast the spices, return the pork, and add the sauce and remaining broth.
Cover and simmer low until the pork is fork-tender.
Weigh the pot, subtract the empty weight, and divide across 14 containers.
